set.body:
Why
Further optimization needs stable, public-workload evidence on both runtimes. The existing JVM NumPy matrix is broad, while the Scala.js probe covers only Double addition and cannot judge the next frontier.

Scope
- Refresh the full public JVM operation matrix on a calm host with pinned JDK, NumPy, CPU, warmup, fork, and sampling metadata.
- Extend the full-linked Node court beyond addition to representative comparison, predicate, scalar and broadcast, cast, reduction, unary, in-place, and strided cases. Generate case families from semantic dimensions so future kernels cannot key off benchmark identities.
- Record semantic signatures, logical sizes, layouts, checksums, and every visible loss. Use the same operation definitions across JVM and Scala.js where the APIs overlap.
- Measure repeat distributions and characterize timer and warmup variance before setting Scala.js regression budgets. Browser performance remains a diagnostic sample; browser correctness stays in the standard gate.
- Add allocation evidence on JVM and practical allocation or GC evidence on Node where tooling is reliable.

Acceptance
- Reproducible commands and machine-readable receipts are checked in.
- JVM comparisons remain public API versus idiomatic NumPy with matched semantics and layout. Scala.js compares fullLink output against a same-host pinned-Node baseline, never Node directly against NumPy.
- Exact semantic and layout signatures pass for all cases on JVM and Scala.js.
- At least three sizes and all relevant layout classes prevent single-shape specialization.
- The court reports geomeans plus individual regressions and does not average away failures.
- Existing JVM and Scala.js test, law, and fullLink gates pass.
set.title: Establish reproducible JVM and Scala.js performance courts
